task.title: balanced-brackets
task.statement: The brackets package exposes is_bracket (already implemented) and a stub is_balanced(s). Implement is_balanced(s) so that it returns True when the three kinds of brackets (), [] and {} in the string s are correctly matched and nested, and False otherwise. Characters that are not brackets are ignored. The empty string is balanced. is_balanced must return a bool. Raise TypeError when s is not a string. Do not change is_bracket or the tests.
acceptance_criteria: nested mixed brackets with other characters are balanced: '(a[b]{c})', 'f(x[0], y[1])'

spec.restated_task: Implement the `is_balanced(s)` function in `brackets/core.py` to return True if the string `s` contains correctly matched and nested brackets of types `()`, `[]`, `{}`, ignoring all other characters. Return False otherwise. The empty string is balanced. The function must return a bool and raise TypeError if `s` is not a string. Do not modify the existing `is_bracket` function or the test files.

interface_contract.name: is_balanced
interface_contract.behavior: Returns True if all brackets in `s` are properly matched and nested, ignoring non-bracket characters. Returns False otherwise. Empty string returns True.
error_cases: TypeError if `s` is not a string

acceptance_criteria: Nested mixed brackets with other characters '(a[b]{c})' and 'f(x[0], y[1])' return True.
Non-bracket characters are ignored (they do not affect bracket matching).
Function returns a bool (True/False) for valid string inputs.
Function raises TypeError when input is not a string (e.g., int, list, None).
out_of_scope: Do not modify the test files (`tests/test_basic.py`, `tests/__init__.py`).
Do not change the public exports of the `brackets` module beyond implementing `is_balanced`.
Do not alter the existing constants `PAIRS`, `OPEN`, `CLOSE` unless necessary for the implementation (they are provided for use).

limitations: Profile 'eval-attest': inference provider nebius_tokenfactory; submission runs must use NVIDIA Nemotron on Nebius Token Factory and are labeled separately.

Sealed and adversarial suites run one child process per test under a supervisor that never imports candidate code; a candidate can still tamper from inside a child after the nonce was read (the mutation gate and held-out tests are the structural detectors).

Model-written sealed and adversarial tests can be wrong; their failures block VERIFIED. An independent arbiter then classifies each failure (implementation bug, test defect or contract dispute) and, for pure test defects, corrects and re-verifies them (must pass on the candidate and still fail on the base). Arbitration is advisory by default and never clears an implementation bug or a contract dispute; it changes the verdict only in explicit apply mode.
Grounding runs only when the specification names external references; sources are cited, not verified for correctness.
Sandbox CPU/RAM quota controls were not found in the current public REST API; per operation only max_layer_bytes, a timeout and the networking flag are set.
Sandbox raw 'cost' diagnostics are not USD; Codex gateway usage is ChatGPT allowance, not a Nebius charge; Nebius USD is computed from the public price table, not an invoice.
Each run retains one checkpoint image on the service; no image-delete control was found in the current public REST API.
